#47
L: By me, gracious, this supreme form has been shown to you, Arjuna, through my own power of yoga: blazing, universal, endless, primal — which, by anyone other than you, has never before been seen.
I: Pleased with you, Arjuna, I have shown you, through my own yogic power, this supreme form — blazing, boundless, without beginning — which no one but you has ever seen before.
N: The chapter's resolution begins: Kṛṣṇa explains that the vision (rūpam ... darśitam, 'the form has been shown') came through ātma-yogāt, 'my own [power of] yoga' — an unearned gift to Arjuna, not something he attained himself. Ātma-yoga here names Kṛṣṇa's own supernatural capacity, not the disciplined practice yoga usually names elsewhere in the poem. Sandhi: तवार्जुनेदं packs tava + arjuna (a + a → ā) + arjuna + idam (a + i → e); यन्मे is yat + me (-t + m- → -n m-, the same assimilation as tat me → tan me at 1.46).
#48
L: Not by study-of-the-Vedas-and-sacrifice, not by gifts, not by rituals, not by fierce austerities, of such a form am I able, in the world of men, to be seen by anyone other than you, O hero of the Kurus.
I: Not by studying the Vedas or by sacrifice, not by giving gifts, not by rites, not by the fiercest austerities can I, in such a form, be seen in the world of men by anyone but you, mighty hero of the Kurus.
N: This verse spans the printed page: the Wikisource line ends दानै- and the next begins र्न, splitting the single sandhi-word dānaiḥ + na ('by gifts' + 'not') across the pāda break, exactly as sura-indra-loka- / m aśnanti was split at ch09 v.20; the entries here follow that precedent, tiling the source exactly and dividing the reading across the two tokens (dānai- / ḥ na). The verse repeats na four times, once before each instrumental (veda-yajña-adhyayanaiḥ, dānaiḥ, kriyābhiḥ, tapobhiḥ) — a standard anaphora of negation. Śakyaḥ ... draṣṭum is a gerundive-plus-infinitive construction, 'is able to be seen'; here and again in v.54, śakya's own visarga drops before the following aham without the usual guṇa to -o (contrast samo 'ham at 9.29) — an epic-Sanskrit metrical variant, not the regular rule.
#49
L: Let there not be fear of yours, nor confusion, at having seen this terrible form of mine, such as this; fear gone, mind glad, again you — that very form of mine, this, behold!
I: Do not be afraid, and do not be bewildered at having seen this terrible form of mine. Be free of fear again, your mind at ease: look, here is that same form of mine once more.
N: Mā with an understood verb of being is the standard Sanskrit prohibitive: te vyathā mā [bhūt], 'let there not be fear of yours'. Vimūḍha-bhāva and vyapeta-bhīḥ / prīta-manāḥ are bahuvrīhi compounds naming Arjuna's state, first terrified and then restored. Sandhi: विमूढभावो is vimūḍha-bhāvaḥ, -aḥ before d- → -o; घोरमीदृङ्ममेदम् packs ghoram + īdṛś (the stem's -ś reverting to its velar allomorph -k, then assimilating to -ṅ before the nasal m- of mama) + mama + idam (a + i → e); पुनस्त्वं is punaḥ + tvam (-aḥ + t- → -as t-, as in duryodhanas tadā at 1.2); तदेव is tat + eva (-t + e- → -d e-).
#50
L: Thus to Arjuna, Vāsudeva having so spoken, his own form he displayed again; and comforted him, frightened, having become again gentle-bodied, the great-souled one.
I: Sañjaya said: Having spoken thus to Arjuna, Vāsudeva showed his own form once more, and comforted him in his fright, becoming again the great-souled one of gentle body.
N: The narrator's voice returns to close the theophany, as it did at the end of chapter 1. Vāsudeva, 'son of Vasudeva', is Kṛṣṇa's patronymic. Darśayāmāsa and āśvāsayāmāsa are both periphrastic perfects (root + -ām + āsa 'did'), the regular way Sanskrit forms the perfect tense of causative verbs. Saumya-vapuḥ mahātmā, 'gentle-bodied, great-souled', marks Kṛṣṇa's return to his familiar human form after the terrifying cosmic one. Sandhi: इत्यर्जुनं is iti + arjunam (-i + a- → -y a-); वासुदेवस्तथोक्त्वा packs vāsudevaḥ + tathā (-aḥ + t- → -as t-) + tathā + uktvā (ā + u → o); सौम्यवपुर्महात्मा is saumya-vapuḥ + mahā-ātmā (-uḥ + m- → -ur m-, the same visarga sandhi as before a vowel, e.g. yajur eva at 9.17, here before a voiced consonant instead).
#51
L: Having seen this human form of yours, gentle, O Janārdana, now I am become composed-minded, returned to [my own] nature.
I: Arjuna said: Seeing this human form of yours again, gentle Janārdana, I have come back to myself; my mind is calm, and I am restored to my own nature.
N: The meter returns here to the two-line anuṣṭubh/śloka that carries the rest of the poem, after the four-line triṣṭubh of verses 47-50 that marked the theophany's high point. Saṃvṛttaḥ ... prakṛtim gataḥ, 'become ... gone to [my own] nature', echoes language used elsewhere in the poem for cosmic dissolution and return, now applied to Arjuna's return to himself. Sandhi: दृष्ट्वेदं is dṛṣṭvā + idam (ā + i → e); इदानीमस्मि is idānīm + asmi, joined without change.
#52
L: Very-hard-to-see is this form which of mine you have seen; the gods too, of this form, always, are longing-to-see.
I: The Blessed Lord said: This form of mine that you have seen is very hard to see; even the gods are forever longing to behold it.
N: Kṛṣṇa begins the chapter's closing teaching on how the cosmic form is, and is not, to be reached. Su-durdarśam stacks two prefixes on darśa 'sight' — su- intensifying, dur- 'hard' — for 'extremely hard to see'. Dṛṣṭavān asi is a periphrastic perfect, 'you have seen' (participle dṛṣṭavān + auxiliary asi), repeated in the next verse. Sandhi: सुदुर्दर्शमिदं is su-durdarśam + idam, joined without change; यन्मम is yat + mama (-t + m- → -n m-, as in yan me at v.47); देवा अप्यस्य is devāḥ + api (an -āḥ ending simply loses its visarga before any vowel, with no merger, unlike the -aḥ-before-a rule seen with śakya in v.48) + api + asya (-i + a- → -y a-).
#53
L: Not I by the Vedas, not by austerity, not by gift-giving, and not by sacrifice; able, of such a kind, to be seen, as you have seen me.
I: Not by the Vedas, not by austerity, not by giving, and not by sacrifice can I be seen — only as you have seen me.
N: This verse restates verse 48's fourfold denial from the far side of the vision, now naming ijyā 'sacrifice, worship' in place of that verse's kriyā 'ritual act'. Evaṃvidhaḥ draṣṭum, 'to be seen in such a manner', picks up evaṃrūpaḥ ... draṣṭum from v.48 almost word for word. Sandhi: नाहं is na + aham (a + a → ā); वेदैर्न is vedaiḥ + na (-aiḥ + n- → -air n-, as in veda-yajña-adhyayanaiḥ na at v.48); चेज्यया is ca + ijyayā (a + i → e); in शक्य एवंविधो, śakyaḥ's visarga drops regularly before the vowel e- of evaṃvidhaḥ — the ordinary rule for -aḥ before a non-a vowel, unlike the anomalous śakya aham of v.48 and v.54.
#54
L: By devotion, but, undivided, able am I, of such a kind, Arjuna, to be known, and to be seen in [my true] reality, and to be entered, O scorcher of the foe.
I: But through devotion that turns nowhere else, Arjuna, I can, in such a form, be known and seen in truth and entered into, scorcher of the foe.
N: The chapter's answer to its own riddle: what the Vedas, austerity, gift-giving and sacrifice cannot reach, ananyayā bhaktyā, 'undivided devotion', does. Bhakti is translated here as 'devotion' rather than left untranslated, since it is not on conventions.md's list of untranslated terms (dharma, yoga, brahman, the guṇas, sāṃkhya) — a choice worth revisiting once ch.12, named for it (Bhaktiyoga), is reached. Three infinitives share the one śakya: jñātum 'to know', draṣṭum 'to see', praveṣṭum 'to enter'. Sandhi: त्वनन्यया is tu + ananyayā (u + a → va, yaṇ sandhi); अहमेवंविधोऽर्जुन packs aham + evaṃvidhaḥ (joined without change) + evaṃvidhaḥ + arjuna (-aḥ + a- → -o with avagraha, the regular pattern — unlike śakya's own irregular elision earlier in the same line).
#55
L: My-work-doing, me-as-highest, my devotee, attachment-free; without hostility toward all beings — who, he comes to me, O son of Pāṇḍu.
I: One who does my work, holds me as the highest goal, is devoted to me, free of attachment, and without hostility toward any being — that one comes to me, Pāṇḍava.
N: The chapter's summary teaching and its closing verse, echoing the four-part formula of 9.34 (man-manāḥ, mad-bhaktaḥ...) but built here as a single relative-correlative sentence (yaḥ ... saḥ, 'who ... he') and ending, as ch.9 does, on the promise of reaching Kṛṣṇa. Bhakti/bhakta are again translated ('devotee') rather than left as bare Sanskrit, matching v.54 and ch.9's practice throughout. Sandhi: मत्कर्मकृन्मत्परमो packs mat-karma-kṛt (mad devoicing to mat- before the voiceless k-, a pattern new in this chapter; contrast mad-bhaktaḥ just after, where mad stays voiced before the voiced bh-) + mat-paramaḥ (kṛt + mat-: -t + m- → -n m-) + mat-paramaḥ + mad-bhaktaḥ (-aḥ before m- → -o); स is saḥ with its visarga dropped before the following consonant, the same pronoun-specific exception already seen at 1.13's sa ghoṣaḥ and 1.19's sa śabdaḥ — saḥ and eṣaḥ drop the visarga before any consonant, not only voiced ones.
